label: digit 0 input at original positions 0-3
explanation: Fires when the input token is the digit 0 during the original phase at positions t=0..3, with zero false positives on dev. Never fires on 0 at original positions >= 4, on any other token, or at the delimiter; only 36 tiny (<0.07 of max) activations in the copy phase when 0 is re-input. Magnitude depends on position: strongest at t=1 (up to max, esp. after first token letters), t=0 ~0.78, t=2 ~0.75, t=3 weakest ~0.3 of max.

issues: The reported test scores of 1.000 are rounded. The real test values are precision 1.0, recall 0.99957, F1 0.99978 and mass recall 0.99998. This is a cosmetic overstatement, not a real gap.

The 29 missed activations on the test split all fall in the copy phase, when a 0 is fed back in, mostly when it recalls original position 3 (recall_idx 4-5). They are tiny (0.02-0.11 of max) and carry 0.0% of the activation mass, so they are noise and not a missing class.
'Never fires on 0 at positions 4 and later' holds: a predicate for 0 at t>=4 in the original phase has precision 0 and recall 0. No other token ever fires, and the delimiter has 0 activations.

The magnitude claims hold. Mean activation at t=3 is about 0.34 of the mean at t=1 (mass share 0.113 vs 0.340 with nearly equal counts). t=1 carries the most mass, and t=0 and t=2 are about 0.8 of t=1.
The label matches the predicate and does not overclaim. No systematic false positives turned up (0 on dev and test), and no length or history pattern was found.
